title: Ukraine arrests four key members of ransomware group that posed as IT support
date_note: Date the National Police published its account; arrest dates are not stated.
geo_basis: agency location; searches in Kyiv and 11 regions
summary: Ukraine's National Police says four key members of an international ransomware group, investigated jointly with the FBI, were served notices of suspicion and are in custody after 66 simultaneous searches. Police say at least 28 companies paid more than $40.5 million in ransom. Callers posed as IT support, using an AI-generated voice platform, to get credentials or remote access.
plain: Police in Ukraine arrested four leaders of a ransomware gang whose members phoned employees pretending to be IT help desk to get in.
exec: Help-desk impersonation by phone remains a working ransomware entry route; callers pushed staff to install remote access tools.
action: Verify callers claiming to be IT support through a known number, and block unapproved remote-access tools.
impact: At least 28 companies paid more than $40.5 million (about UAH 1.8 billion) in ransom per police; one US company paid $5 million after a $10 million demand. Final damage still being established.

validation.note: Police original read, plus Help Net Security's report of it.
